title: The Butterfly Étude across a century
work: Étude in G-flat major, Op. 25 No. 9
question: How do d’Albert, Cortot and Neeman weight the same compact opening figure?
intro: D’Albert’s early Odeon recording and Cortot’s 1920 Victor side are compared with Edward Neeman’s modern Musopen performance. Cortot’s original stream couples the Black Keys Étude first: the Butterfly passage begins around 1:36.5 and has not been cut into a new audio file. D’Albert is mapped only through the shared opening 40 reference seconds because the later path jumps across extra material; no whole-work tempo claim is made from that path. Cortot’s map excludes the noisy tail, and neither historical audio stream is retuned.

recordings.label: Eugen d’Albert, 1912–13
recordings.note: Opening passage only is aligned; later correspondence is unresolved. The complete source file remains playable.

recordings.label: Alfred Cortot, 1920
recordings.note: Butterfly begins around 1:36.5 after Black Keys in the unedited stream; compare only the mapped second-piece passage.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman, c. 2014
recordings.note: Modern reference; loudest five-second window around 0:40, followed by the strongest measured change near 0:48.

passages.label: Opening figure
passages.note: Compare the weight and spacing of the short figure. Cortot starts inside a two-piece disc side, not at the file’s beginning.

passages.label: First measured turn
passages.note: A strong change in the reference provides a provisional shared landmark within the opening passage.

passages.label: Compact contrast
passages.note: Follow the figure through the early contrast; this passage remains within d’Albert’s reliably mapped opening.

passages.label: Central drive
passages.note: Compare the continuity of the central figure without inferring original piano tone from the acoustic transfers.

passages.label: Final turn
passages.note: The reference’s strongest measured change occurs here. Only Cortot and Neeman have a published correspondence this far into the piece.

alignment.scope: d’Albert: reference 0–40 to 0–35.4. Cortot: reference 0–64.5 to 96.5–150. No extrapolation across unresolved later material or noisy tails.
alignment.method: Automatic chroma CENS + DTW; original source files unedited.
